Home.subtitle: Start building your client management system
Home.distinctionExplain:
Units are ranked by a composite distinction score:
1. Total price = down payment + remaining balance
2. Actual price/m² = total price ÷ area
3. Market price/m² per compound (e.g. The Brooks: 36,000, Stone Residence: 34,000)
4. Value ratio = market price/m² ÷ actual price/m²
5. Finishing weight: fully finished = 1.0, semi-finished = 0.7, shell = 0.4
6. Score = value ratio × finishing weight × 100

A high score means you're paying less than the compound's market rate for a well-finished unit.

campaignsCount.title: Campaigns
campaignsCount.what: Total number of ad campaigns the company has registered in the system.
campaignsCount.formula: Number of rows in the campaigns table
campaignsCount.impact: A general indicator of marketing activity volume.
campaignsCount.impactUp: More concurrent campaigns = channel diversification and greater reach.
campaignsCount.impactDown: Fewer campaigns = more focus or a quieter marketing period.

totalSpend.title: Total Spend
totalSpend.what: Sum of the costs of all registered ad campaigns (entered by the manager when creating each campaign).
totalSpend.formula: Sum of each campaign's total cost
totalSpend.example: Two campaigns costing 10,000 and 5,000 = 15,000 total spend
totalSpend.impact: This is the denominator in ROI and cost-per-client formulas.
totalSpend.impactUp: Higher spend must be matched by more clients or deals, otherwise profitability suffers.
totalSpend.impactDown: Lower spend = lower risk, but possibly slower growth.

totalNetProfit.title: Total Net Profit
totalNetProfit.what: Company's total net profit from all deals linked to all campaigns, minus total campaign costs.
totalNetProfit.formula: Sum (company net profit of linked deals) − Sum (campaign costs)
totalNetProfit.example: Linked deals with 20,000 net profit and 12,000 campaign costs = 8,000 net profit
totalNetProfit.impact: The final verdict on overall marketing profitability.
totalNetProfit.impactUp: Positive and rising = marketing is generating real returns.
totalNetProfit.impactDown: Negative = campaign costs exceed the profit they generate.

overallRoi.title: Overall ROI
overallRoi.what: Profit ratio for every currency unit spent across all campaigns combined.
overallRoi.impact: The higher it is above zero, the more profitable marketing is overall.
overallRoi.impactUp: Above zero and rising = excellent return on spent money.

totalClients.title: Total Clients
totalClients.what: Number of clients (company clients) linked to ad campaigns.
totalClients.formula: Sum of clients linked to each campaign
totalClients.example: One campaign brought 30 clients and another 20 = 50 total
totalClients.impact: The size of the marketing opportunity funnel.
totalClients.impactUp: More qualified clients coming from ads.
totalClients.impactDown: Fewer clients from campaigns = weak targeting or low attraction.

totalDeals.title: Total Deals
totalDeals.what: Number of financial deals (recorded in finances) linked to ad campaigns.
totalDeals.formula: Sum of deals linked to each campaign
totalDeals.example: 3 deals from one campaign + 2 from another = 5 deals
totalDeals.impact: The final outcome marketing converts into income.
totalDeals.impactUp: More completed deals from ad-driven clients.
totalDeals.impactDown: Few deals despite many clients = conversion or follow-up problem.

clientsCount.title: Clients
clientsCount.what: Number of company clients linked to this campaign (linked by the manager from the company clients page).
clientsCount.formula: Number of client rows where ad_campaign_id = this campaign
clientsCount.impactDown: Fewer clients = consider adjusting targeting or raising budget.

dealsCount.title: Deals
dealsCount.what: Number of financial deals linked to this campaign (linked by the manager from the finances page).
dealsCount.formula: Number of deal rows where ad_campaign_id = this campaign
dealsCount.impactUp: More deals from the same campaign = real success.
dealsCount.impactDown: Fewer deals = campaign attracts low-seriousness clients.

commission.title: Commissions
commission.what: Sum of final commissions of the deals linked to the campaign — the campaign's revenue before expenses.
commission.formula: Sum of final commissions of linked deals
commission.impactDown: Lower revenue = smaller or fewer deals.

netProfit.title: Net Profit
netProfit.what: Company's net profit from the deals linked to the campaign (after deducting employee shares, nathryat and deal expenses) minus the campaign cost.
netProfit.formula: Net Profit = Sum (company net profit of linked deals) − Campaign cost
netProfit.example: 3 deals with 8,000 + 5,000 + 4,000 = 17,000 net profit, campaign cost 12,000 → net profit 5,000
netProfit.impact: The final answer: is the campaign profitable or not?
netProfit.impactUp: Positive = campaign covered its cost and generated profit.
netProfit.impactDown: Negative = campaign costs more than it returns.

roi.title: Return on Investment (ROI)
roi.what: A measure that tells you how much net profit every spent unit returns.
roi.example: A campaign costing 10,000 generated 5,000 net profit → ROI = (5,000 ÷ 10,000) × 100 = 50%
roi.impact: When the cost is zero a dash (—) is shown because division is undefined.
roi.impactUp: Higher = each spent unit returns more profit. This is the main goal.
roi.impactDown: Below zero = the campaign is losing money.

cpa.title: Cost Per Acquisition (CPA)
cpa.what: Average cost to acquire one new client from the campaign.
cpa.formula: CPA = Campaign cost ÷ Number of linked clients
cpa.example: A 10,000 campaign brought 50 clients → CPA = 10,000 ÷ 50 = 200 per client
cpa.impact: Important to compare it with the average client value.
cpa.impactUp: Rising = less efficient targeting or an exhausted audience.
cpa.impactDown: Falling = the campaign acquires clients cheaper, which is excellent.

costPerDeal.title: Cost Per Deal
costPerDeal.what: Cost to complete a single deal among the deals linked to the campaign.
costPerDeal.formula: Cost per deal = Campaign cost ÷ Number of linked deals
costPerDeal.example: A 12,000 campaign generated 4 deals → cost per deal = 12,000 ÷ 4 = 3,000
costPerDeal.impact: The lower it is compared to per-deal net profit, the more viable the campaign.
costPerDeal.impactUp: Higher than per-deal profit = losing money per deal.
costPerDeal.impactDown: Lower = each completed deal costs less.

conversionRate.title: Conversion Rate
conversionRate.what: Percentage of clients linked to the campaign who actually converted into deals.
conversionRate.formula: Conversion Rate = (Number of deals ÷ Number of clients) × 100
conversionRate.example: 50 clients, 5 of them made a deal → Conversion Rate = (5 ÷ 50) × 100 = 10%
conversionRate.impact: Note: a campaign client may convert months later, not immediately.
conversionRate.impactUp: Higher = clients are qualified and convert easily.
conversionRate.impactDown: Lower = weak data/targeting or weak follow-up.

avgRevenuePerClient.title: Average Revenue per Client (ARPU)
avgRevenuePerClient.what: Average revenue (commissions) generated per client coming from the campaign.
avgRevenuePerClient.formula: ARPU = Total linked commissions ÷ Number of linked clients
avgRevenuePerClient.example: 20,000 commissions over 50 clients → ARPU = 400 per client
avgRevenuePerClient.impact: Compare it with the cost per acquisition (CPA).
avgRevenuePerClient.impactUp: Higher than CPA = the campaign is viable at the client level.
avgRevenuePerClient.impactDown: Lower than CPA = you lose money on each acquired client.

avgDealValue.title: Average Deal Value
avgDealValue.what: Average size of the deals linked to the campaign in terms of final commission.
avgDealValue.formula: Average deal value = Total linked commissions ÷ Number of deals
avgDealValue.example: 20,000 commissions over 5 deals → average deal value = 4,000
avgDealValue.impact: Helps compare deal quality across campaigns.
avgDealValue.impactUp: Higher = larger and more valuable deals.

breakEven.title: Break-even Point
breakEven.what: The number of deals needed to fully cover the campaign cost, after which the campaign starts making net profit.
breakEven.formula: Break-even (number of deals) = Campaign cost ÷ Average company net profit per deal
breakEven.example: Cost 12,000 and average net profit per deal 4,000 → need at least 3 deals.
breakEven.impact: Helps you know how many more deals the campaign needs before it stops losing.
breakEven.impactUp: Per-deal net profit rose = break-even drops = faster break-even.
breakEven.impactDown: Average deal profit dropped = need more deals to cover the cost.
